title: Shutter
description: Cumulus crossing a Tokyo sky, seen from the pavement between two towers, on a locked-off time-lapse. Press and hold and the shutter opens on bulb: the frame integrates the light for as long as you hold, so the clouds smear into silk along their real wind while the towers, the lamp post and the trees, which never moved, stay sharp. An ND filter follows the shutter, so the brightness holds and only time grows. Let go and the long exposure stays on the print until the next press.
intent: After Louis Daguerre's Boulevard du Temple (1838, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boulevard_du_Temple_(photograph)): the street in that plate looks empty because the exposure ran for minutes and the walkers and carriages never stayed in one place long enough to register; only a man having his boots polished stood still and was kept. A photograph keeps what stays. Here the exposure is a real temporal integral of recorded frames in linear light, offline-baked as a time pyramid of block means so any open interval is a cheap weighted sum, developed through the summer-film pipeline (factory/reality/techniques.md, piece 1).
sources: Plate: "Time Lapse Footage of a Sky on the City" by Hiro Nakamura (Pexels @tybo), Pexels 5338574, 1920x1080 29.97 fps, 2:02, GoPro time-lapse; Pexels License (free to use, no attribution required). https://www.pexels.com/video/time-lapse-footage-of-a-sky-on-the-city-5338574/ (file: https://videos.pexels.com/video-files/5338574/5338574-hd_1920_1080_30fps.mp4). Used: frames 1300-2499, cropped 3:2 (x 120-1740), stabilised by phase correlation of the building band (it drifts about 0.9 px), graded in OKLab (the source's violet cobalt rotated to cyan-cobalt), looped with a 48-frame linear-light cross-fade. Bake: tools/depth/bakes/shutter/bake.py.
